assessmentSummary.identity: A standing landmine push press from a declared shoulder or two-hand central rack, using a controlled shallow dip and continuous forceful hip-knee-ankle drive into the anchored diagonal press, finishing tall without a second receiving dip or deliberate foot relocation, then returning under control.
currentCardFindings: Migration 388 already consolidates the former Two-Hand Landmine Push Press source into this survivor and renames the display identity Landmine Push Press, but the surviving card still needs exact hand-count variants and full structural content.

One-hand and two-hand execution are exact variants of the same dip-drive press identity; hand count changes symmetry, trunk demand, load tolerance, stance, and side dosage rather than the ordered action.
Push jerk, split jerk, squat-to-press, rotational press, clean-to-press, and strict press change receiving action or ordered movement and remain separate identities.

variantDifficultyCandidates.basis: unilateral rack and square lower-body drive add anti-rotation and side-dose demands
a declared stagger changes force symmetry and coordination while preserving the no-step push-press sequence
two-hand symmetry reduces anti-rotation but permits greater external load

proposedDeliveryProfiles.purpose: Develop repeatable lower-to-upper force transfer and diagonal pressing velocity before fatigue.
Build load tolerance in the fixed dip-drive sequence without turning the set into conditioning.

coach: Verify anchor, collars, load, rack, hand count, stance, side sequence, and lane clearance.
Require a shallow vertical dip, whole-foot pressure, continuous drive into the bar, and no second receiving dip.
End the set when timing, speed, finish, side balance, or controlled return changes.
athlete: Set the bar at the declared rack and brace before moving.
Dip straight down a little, drive the floor away, and send that force through the sleeve.
Finish tall without stepping or dipping again, then lower to the same rack under control.

assessmentSummary.identity: A unilateral landmine jerk beginning from a declared shoulder rack and bilateral start, using a controlled dip and explosive drive, then rapidly splitting the feet to receive and stabilize the bar with the working arm extended before a declared recovery sequence and controlled return.
currentCardFindings: The existing card is generic landmine language and does not declare the split receiving phase, lead-leg relationship, recovery order, catch ownership, or failed-repetition response.
The working-arm-to-lead-leg relationship must be explicit because it changes cross-body stabilization and side-dose accounting.
A push press has no receiving split; a fixed split-stance press starts in the split; neither is an interchangeable label for this jerk.

assessmentSummary.identity: A landmine squat-to-press beginning with the sleeve at a declared chest or shoulder rack, descending through a deliberate squat to an owned depth, then standing and continuously transferring lower-body force into the anchored diagonal press before a controlled return to the rack.
